Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings, reasoning, and impressions: 
  - Patient reports ~2 months of progressive anxiety temporally related to starting a new, stressful job. Symptoms include morning anticipatory panic, irregular rapid palpitations (minutes), poor sleep (~3–4 hours/night), daytime fatigue, anhedonia, social avoidance, and reduced activity. No suicidal ideation. Lives with family; willing to engage in talking therapy. Clinician recommended self-referral to talking therapy resources and basic blood tests with GP follow-up.  
  - DDx supports a primary stress-related/psychiatric cause given the clear temporal relation to a psychosocial stressor and symptom pattern, while also identifying cardiac and endocrine causes to exclude because of prominent palpitations and poor sleep.  
- Relevant differentials from DDx that support/refine clinician impression: 
  - Adjustment disorder with anxiety — primary working consideration given temporal relation to new job and symptoms focused on that stressor.  
  - Generalized anxiety disorder — possible but duration (~2 months) is less than 6 months required for GAD diagnosis; consider if symptoms persist.  
  - Paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (e.g., SVT/AF) — plausible explanation for irregular palpitations; cannot be excluded without ECG/monitoring.  
  - Hyperthyroidism and substance-related causes (alcohol/caffeine/nicotine) — possible reversible causes to screen with blood tests and substance history.  
- Working diagnosis: 
  - Adjustment disorder with anxiety (work-related).  
    - Justification: onset ~2 months after starting a new, stressful job with symptoms primarily focused around work situations, causing functional impairment (sleep disruption, reduced enjoyment, avoidance). DDx ranks this as High likelihood and is consistent with transcript.  
- Considerations (additional plausible but uncertain options from DDx): 
  - Generalized anxiety disorder (Medium likelihood) — consider if symptoms persist ≥6 months or become more pervasive.  
  - Paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (Medium likelihood) — palpitations irregular and episodic; consider ECG/ambulatory rhythm monitoring if symptoms persist or if clinical concern increases.  
  - Hyperthyroidism or other endocrine/metabolic causes (Low–Medium) — blood tests recommended to exclude.  
  - Substance-related contributors (Low) — alcohol patterns and occasional smoking could contribute; assess quantity/timing and consider brief intervention if relevant.  
- Management plan documented in transcript: 
  - Mental health: Patient encouraged to self-refer to NHS talking therapy (IAPT) and clinician to send link/online resources; patient agreeable to one-to-one therapy.  
  - Investigations: Arrange basic blood tests (clinician recommended) to exclude biochemical triggers; patient instructed to call support line to arrange tests.  
  - Follow-up: GP follow-up arranged approximately one week after blood tests to review results (clinician recommended).  
  - Safety: Patient has family support; no suicidal ideation; advised to re-contact if symptoms worsen or if unable to cope with work/ADLs.  
  - Medication: Clinician advised medications are not first-line at this stage; not prescribed in this consultation.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment disorder with anxiety — High. 
  - Justification: Symptoms began ~2 months after starting a stressful new job, are focused on work-related situations, and cause functional impairment; DDx ranked this highest and this matches the transcript.  
- Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) — Medium. 
  - Justification: Clinical features (excessive worry, insomnia, fatigue, anhedonia) are consistent with GAD, but duration is ~2 months (<6 months threshold), making GAD less likely now but possible if symptoms persist.  
- Paroxysmal cardiac arrhythmia (e.g., SVT or AF) — Medium. 
  - Justification: Irregular, rapid palpitations lasting minutes to ~10 minutes are compatible with paroxysmal arrhythmia; cannot be excluded without ECG/ambulatory monitoring.
